The current left lower leg on screen LEFT is supporting and right leg screen RIGHT is bent up, which is the wrong half-cycle. Draw the opposite: anatomical RIGHT leg on SCREEN RIGHT descends from the right hip and its blue boot is planted at x approximately 695,y1165, pointing upper-left. Anatomical LEFT leg from LEFT jade hip bends BACK toward lower-left; its lifted blue boot at x approximately430,y1080 exposes its tan sole to viewer. Keep thighs anatomically attached to their own hips; do not cross legs, do not mirror. We must see ONE planted RIGHT boot on screen RIGHT and ONE bent-back airborne LEFT boot on screen LEFT. Open white trousers separate, knees and ankles legible. The planted boot has heel and front sole visibly flat on its local ground plane; upper body same slight lean. Right fan arm stays behind on screen right, left empty arm stays front on screenleft. Preserve native1254 square transparent RGBA, fixed camera/root, no whole image scaling/reposition, no ground shadow or effects.
